issues.title: Introduce a Batch Authorization Identifier to Link the Batch Token and Derived Downscoped Tokens
issues.author: NiYuan224
issues.body:
The draft does not define a common identifier linking Downscoped Tokens derived from the same Batch Token.

A common identifier would enable:

1. Token correlation: Identify all Downscoped Tokens derived from the same batch authorization.
2. Shared constraints: Associate multiple Downscoped Tokens with common authorization constraints. For example, in UC8 of [draft-chen-oauth-agent-authz-use-cases](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-chen-oauth-agent-authz-use-cases-04#section-4.2.3), a travel assistant delegates flight and hotel bookings to separate agents under a total budget of 100. A common identifier would allow both tokens to reference the same budget constraint.
3. Batch revocation: Identify all affected Downscoped Tokens when the batch authorization is revoked.


### TODO
Introduce a `batch_id` claim in the Batch Token and require the AS to associate each derived Downscoped Token with the same `batch_id` during Token Exchange. For JWT Downscoped Tokens, the `batch_id` claim can be included directly; for other token formats, the AS can maintain an equivalent association.

issues.title: Clarify Authorization Remediation During Delegated Task Execution
issues.author: NiYuan224
issues.body:
During the 10.19 OAuth WG interim meeting, WG co-chair Hannes Tschofenig raised the question of how a Sub-Client should obtain additional authorization when its existing permissions are insufficient: should it request authorization directly or ask the Leader-Client to coordinate the request?

I believe this is a general issue in delegated interactions, including client-to-agent and agent-to-agent scenarios.

A2A [Section 7.6](https://github.com/a2aproject/A2A/blob/main/docs/specification.md#76-in-task-authorization) supports both direct authorization and requesting assistance from an upstream client , including further propagation through agent chains. 

##TODO

Clarify that a Sub-Client may request additional authorization directly or seek assistance from the Leader-Client, following the approaches described in A2A. The mechanism for propagating additional authorization requirements across delegation relationships is outside the scope of this document and may be addressed in a separate document.

pulls.title: Clarify Token Exchange Processing and Token Lifetime Requirements
pulls.author: NiYuan224
pulls.body:
This PR clarifies the Batch Token and Downscoped Token processing rules.

1. Define the Batch Token expiration as the lifetime of the batch authorization.
2. Clarify Batch Token validation and Sub-Client authentication methods.
3. Clarify optional actor_token validation and may_act.sub matching during token exchange.
4. Require Downscoped Tokens to expire no later than the Batch Token.
5. Update the corresponding token exchange examples.

pulls.title: Introduce a Batch Authorization Identifier to Link the Batch Token and Derived Downscoped Tokens
pulls.author: NiYuan224
pulls.body:
This PR addresses Issue #2 by introducing a `batch_id` to associate Downscoped Tokens derived from the same batch authorization.

The changes:

1. Define the `batch_id` claim in the Batch Token and require the same identifier to be associated with all derived Downscoped Tokens.

2. Require the AS to use the same `batch_id` from the Batch Token in all derived Downscoped Tokens. For JWT Downscoped Tokens, the AS MUST include the `batch_id` claim with the same value as in the Batch Token; for non-JWT tokens, the AS MUST maintain an equivalent association. The AS MUST enforce shared constraints across all relevant Downscoped Tokens associated with the same `batch_id`.

3. Add Security Considerations describing how `batch_id` supports identifying affected Downscoped Tokens when a batch authorization is revoked.
